slot.brief: Solve a simple trigonometric equation of the form sin θ = given value and write the general solution.

stem: The general solution of the trigonometric equation $2\sin\left(2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1$, where $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, is

verdicts.working: sin(2θ−π/4)=1/2 ⇒ 2θ−π/4 = nπ+(−1)^n π/6 ⇒ θ = nπ/2 + π/8 + (−1)^n π/12. Numerical check confirms option B satisfies the equation for all tested n; A, C, D fail.

working:
Given equation:
$$2\sin\left(2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1$$
$$\implies \sin\left(2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$$
Since $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, the general solution of $\sin X = \sin\alpha$ is $X = n\pi + (-1)^n \alpha$, where $n \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Setting $X = 2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ and $\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$:
$$2\theta - \dfrac{\pi}{4} = n\pi + (-1)^n \dfrac{\pi}{6}$$
$$2\theta = n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{4} + (-1)^n \dfrac{\pi}{6}$$
Dividing by $2$:
$$\theta = \dfrac{n\pi}{2} + \dfrac{\pi}{8} + (-1)^n \dfrac{\pi}{12}$$

Independent check: sin(2θ−π/4)=1/2 ⇒ 2θ−π/4 = nπ+(−1)^n π/6 ⇒ θ = nπ/2 + π/8 + (−1)^n π/12. Numerical check confirms option B satisfies the equation for all tested n; A, C, D fail.

draft.distractor_notes:
Option A encodes a sign error when moving $-\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ to the right-hand side.
Option C comes from forgetting to divide the phase shift $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ by $2$ when solving for $\theta$.
Option D results from confusing the special angles of sine and cosine, using $\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ to obtain $\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$ and $\dfrac{\alpha}{2} = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$.
